findings.title: Call, hidden voice, and confidential relay
findings.claim: Within the pericope, a message can move from raised calling and uncertain prophetic sound through confidential counsel into a written and messenger-borne relay, while the focus tongue supplies the receiving and onward-speaking medium.
findings.mechanism: The focus lisan carrier at 19:50:7:1 contacts the raised call at 19:52:1, private counsel at 19:52:7, prophetic sound at 19:51:10, messenger speech at 19:51:9, and Book writing at 19:51:3; these distinct carriers make low or private speech newly readable as transmissive rather than lost at its first audience.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus tongue becomes a relay that preserves the force of both public proclamation and confidential address across speakers, records, and audiences.
findings.containment: This is a bounded pericope-level relay image. It does not claim that every prophetic designation lexically means sound, that private counsel is publicly loud, or that the listed source images form a single lexical sense.

epistemic.reason: The channel support is trusted and every carrier returns through a supplied focus occurrence, but several non-focus branches are source semantic images rather than independently resolved lexical senses in those occurrences.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The lofty tongue can be heard as part of a messenger-borne transmission rather than only as a favorable label.
branch_activations.boundary: No claim is made that the focus noun itself lexically means messenger or that every named prophet is a separate messenger activation.

findings.title: Well-hoist assembly
findings.claim: The pericope's focus on an elevated result can be pictured, at an exploratory macro level, as the raised bearing of a hoist that draws an otherwise inaccessible provision into reach.
findings.mechanism: The focus high-position carrier at 19:50:9:1 contacts the context images of a well weight at 19:46:10, long rope at 19:44:4, lifting cord at 19:57:1, handled bucket at 19:47:2, and bucket loop at 19:42:9; their separate tool carriers form a coherent lift from below to above and return through the focus adjective.
findings.reader_payoff: Elevation becomes a concrete relation of bearing, tension, drawing, and reception rather than a static status word alone.
findings.containment: This remains a source-image assembly and does not claim that the focus adjective lexically names a tool, bucket, rope, or physical lifting operation. The pericope's prophetic and gift readings remain intact.

epistemic.reason: The channel and branch nominations are trusted, but the hoist is an analogical construction from source semantic images rather than a directly stated pericope mechanism.

findings.title: Promise fulfilled into durable public reputation
findings.claim: The pericope lets the focus phrase hold together truthful speech, fulfilled expectation, complete reliability, and a durable public report, so elevated truth appears as a reputation made credible by conduct and preserved in speech.
findings.mechanism: The focus truth carrier at 19:50:8:1 contacts the promise at 19:54:8, the straight-path trigger at 19:43:13, and the repeated truthful identities at 19:41:7 and 19:56:7; the focus tongue's speech and public-praise facets then meet the Book remembrance and the report-raised image to turn truth from a label into a temporally tested legacy.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why the elevated tongue is both reliable and remembered: promise is enacted, character is recognized, and speech carries the result onward.
findings.containment: The physical-straightness branch is retained only through the supplied straightness contact as a source variant; it is not a claim that the tongue is a physical object. The finding does not select between truthful speech, reliable character, fulfilled promise, and public reputation.

epistemic.reason: Trusted support, repeated pericope carriers, and exact focus returns directly establish the bounded relation, while the source-variant and public-report facets remain explicitly contained.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees how a verbal legacy can remain alive without being merely ephemeral: repetition gives it voice, the Book gives it a durable register, and truthful worth gives it content.
findings.containment: This is attributed contextual evidence from a legacy-unbound HFT record. The unresolved branches receive no invented gloss or facet, and the registered focus branches are used only for the supplied contextual relation; the finding does not claim a verified lexical equivalence between any unresolved branch and its role.

epistemic.reason: The HFT record has exact supplied Arabic anchors and complete pericope scope, but its segmentation, roots, branch identities, and roles remain attributed rather than independently verified.

findings.title: Rejection raised into public voice
findings.claim: The attributed pericope sequence allows the lofty tongue to function as a social reversal: speech threatened with coercive silencing is followed by separation, gift, and raised public authority.
findings.mechanism: The HFT trace connects the stoning threat at 19:46:10 and imposed separation at 19:46:11 to withdrawal at 19:49:2, gift at 19:49:8, the focus tongue at 19:50:7:1, and explicit raising at 19:57:1; the ordered contacts turn elevation into a changed reading of what happens after rejection.
findings.reader_payoff: The later lofty voice becomes perceptible as an answer to attempted marginalization, not only as an isolated honor attached to the gifts.
findings.containment: This is qualified attributed contextual evidence. It preserves the live alternative that the gifts and honors simply follow separation without specifically answering the speech conflict, and it does not assert a verified lexical branch for unresolved HFT records.

epistemic.reason: Exact pericope Arabic anchors and a complete attributed sequence support the before-and-after relation, but the HFT source is legacy-unbound and its root and role assignments are not independently established here.

findings.title: Kin-distributed tongue
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the singular truthful tongue assigned for the plural group can image a shared voice carried through kinship, related prophetic recipients, descendants, and renewed recitation.
findings.mechanism: The attributed HFT trace returns from mercy's kinship carrier at 19:50:4:1 and the focus lisan at 19:50:7:1 through the brother gift at 19:53:1 and 19:53:5, descendant spreading at 19:58:9 and 19:58:16, truthful worth at 19:50:8:1, and recitation at 19:58:23; the contacts change an individual-praise reading into a bounded social-medium image.
findings.reader_payoff: The plural pronoun and singular tongue become newly perceptible as a shared medium that can travel through related recipients without requiring one isolated speaker.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory social metaphor from a legacy-unbound HFT record. It does not claim that lisan lexically means lineage, that kinship is the ordinary sense of mercy here, or that the shared-voice image displaces the ordinary truthful reputation reading.

epistemic.reason: The exact supplied anchors and attributed trace form a coherent contact network, but the record itself labels the inference exploratory and provides no independent lexical branch records for several carriers.

friction_notes: The explicitly added 1:2-1:7 overlay was reviewed only after the native and pericope phase. Its repeated mercy, praise, lordship, guidance, and path material supplied no non-duplicative local carrier-trigger-focus return, so no external overlay finding is retained.

The HFT records are legacy_unbound: their exact supplied Arabic anchors and stated coordinate roles remain visible as attributed evidence, while unresolved branch identities receive no invented gloss or facet.
